2014_059_020414mtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education held February 4, 2014 at Troy High School, combining athletic and staff recognitions, five sets of January 2014 minutes, the December 2013 Treasurer's Report with its full check register and wire-transfer listing, a new-hire personnel item, a STANFRED Consultants enrollment-projection report, and two business actions. The largest decision before the board was the award of a school-bus purchase to Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) in the amount of $1,659,011.00, charged to the 2014 Capital Projects Fund. December 2013 total disbursements in the period were reported at $6,146,830.53.
2014_059_020414mtg.page:
**Meeting.** Regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, 7:00 PM, February 4, 2014, Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy., Troy, MI 48098. District offices: 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000; meetings cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and streamed at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** Senior Scholar Athletes 2013-14 (certificates for athletes maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average); six fall All-State athletes -- Luis Anaya, Aaron Gebauer and Bryan Lawson (Athens boys soccer, coach Todd Heugh), Abby Green (Troy High cross country, coach Matt Richardson), Jennifer Yang (Athens girls golf, coach Dan Cooper) and Richard Zhang (Athens boys tennis, coach Andrew Shipp); a resolution naming February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy; and a $5,000 check from Enviro-Clean Maintenance Services (John Thompson, Craig Wyse) to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, accepted by TFEE president Al Robinson.

**January minutes.** The January 14, 2014 organizational meeting at Athens High School elected Ms. Philippart president (14-002), Mr. Miletti vice president (14-003) and Mr. Schmidt secretary (14-004) through December 31, 2014, all 7-0, and appointed Mark S. Rajter treasurer for January through December 2014 (14-005). Resolution 14-006 designated depositories including Bank of America, Comerica, Fifth Third, Flagstar Bancorp, JP Morgan Chase, PNC Bank and MILAF, with investments governed by Board Policy D-1103 and Section 380.1223(1)(h) of the Revised School Code. The January 14 regular meeting drew roughly 125 people, nearly all speaking on the teachers' pay freeze and ongoing negotiations, and adopted four Schools of Choice resolutions (14-011 through 14-014) under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act for 2014-2015: 50 nonresident kindergarten and 25 first-grade seats, plus 26 seats in grades 6-8 at Baker Middle School.

**General Fund (101, 120, 122), December year to date, FY2014.** Revenue: approved budget $132,247,089, actual $44,488,041, uncollected $87,759,048 (66.36%). Expenditures: approved $131,805,201, actual $50,080,267, encumbered $4,452,437, available $77,272,497 (58.63%). Excess revenue over expenditures 441,888; fund balance December 1, 2013 of 22,070,236 and fund balance June 30, 2014 of $22,512,124. Debt Service Funds (304, 306, 307, 312) show property taxes of 16,145,934 budgeted against 8,427,849 actual and a fund balance moving from (2,938,785) to $923,037.

**Check register.** Pentamation report ACCTPA21, run 01/10/2014, accounting period 7/14, covering checks dated 12/01/2013 through 12/31/2013. Fund totals: General Fund 101 $3,187,240.05; Grant 120 $507.00; Special Education 122 $133,184.17; 2014 Cap Proj Series 1 414 $221,826.60; Food Service 520 $28,538.53; TCC Grant 529 $18,442.54; Continuing Education 530 $4,478.17; Student Activity 700 $123,683.72; Activity 701 $1,668.24; total report $3,719,569.02. Largest single check: MI Educ Spec Serv Assn, $1,857,357.80.

**Personnel and curriculum.** Probationary contract for Danielle Andresen, .5 FTE ESL teacher at Hamilton and Costello Elementary Schools, for the remainder of 2013-2014. Dr. Fowler presented enrollment projections prepared by Dr. Frederick R. Ignatovich of STANFRED Consultants, projecting total K-12 enrollment of 12,653 in 2014/15 and 12,785 in 2018/19.

**Business.** A Section 22f Best Practices resolution certifying compliance with at least 7 of 8 criteria (MCL 388.1622f) to claim the $52 per pupil one-time grant; and award of the bus bid to Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) at $1,659,011.00 against competing quotes of $1,659,658.00 from Capital City (IC) and $1,699,087.00 from Holland (Bluebird). Dr. Fowler also reported the Phase 1 bond project timeline.

**Meeting.** Regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, 7:00 PM, February 4, 2014, Troy High School, 4777 Northfield Pkwy., Troy, MI 48098; district administration at 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) and posted at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognitions.** Certificates for Senior Scholar Athletes 2013-14, students maintaining a 3.5 cumulative grade point average while participating in an athletic program. Mr. Jolly reads biographies of six 2013 fall All-State athletes: Luis Anaya, Aaron Gebauer and Bryan Lawson (Athens boys soccer, coach Todd Heugh), Abby Green (Troy High cross country), Jennifer Yang (Athens girls golf) and Richard Zhang (Athens boys tennis). A resolution recognizes February as Principal Appreciation Month in Troy, and John Thompson and Craig Wyse of Enviro-Clean Maintenance Services present a $5,000 check to the Troy Foundation for Educational Excellence, accepted by TFEE president Al Robinson.

**January minutes.** At the January 14, 2014 organizational meeting at Athens High School (7:02 p.m. to 7:24 p.m., roughly 150 in the audience), motion 14-001 made Ms. Philippart acting chairperson with Judy Holmes temporary secretary; 14-002, 14-003 and 14-004 elected Ms. Philippart president, Mr. Miletti vice president and Mr. Schmidt secretary through December 31, 2014, each 7-0; 14-005 appointed Mark S. Rajter, Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, Treasurer for January through December 2014. Resolution 14-006 designated depositories: Bank of America, Charter One Bank, Bank of New York, JP Morgan Chase Bank, First Merit Bank (formerly Citizen's Bank), Comerica Bank, Fifth Third Bank, Flagstar Bancorp, MILAF through PFM Asset Management and Fifth Third Bank, Morgan Stanley Smith Barney, PFM Securities, and PNC Bank. Checks carry Treasurer Rajter's facsimile signature, with emergency handwritten signature by the Treasurer or Superintendent Barbara A. Fowler on the Bank of America General Fund and Payroll accounts; PNC accounts pay Troy Career Center expenses and a Comerica account pays flexible spending claims by ACH debit to Next Generation Enrollment, Inc.; investments follow Board Policy D-1103 and subsection (1)(h) of Section 380.1223 of the Revised School Code. Motions 14-007 (superintendent as deputy secretary), 14-008 (Judy Holmes to post notices) and 14-009 (2014 meeting calendar) each carried 7-0. Sodexo's Gayle Moran and Hal Davis presented a $500 check to International Academy-East student representative Needa Toofanny for winning the Healthy High School Challenge.

The January 14 regular meeting ran 7:25 p.m. to 10:35 p.m. before roughly 125 people, with extended public comment on the teachers' pay freeze and negotiations, including TEA president Tony Lucchi. Motion 14-010 approved the December 3, 2013 minutes and the November 2013 Treasurer's Report. Motions 14-011 through 14-014 adopted Schools of Choice programs under Sections 105 and 105c of the State School Aid Act of 1979, as amended by Public Act 300 of 1996, for 2014-2015: 50 nonresident kindergarten and 25 nonresident first-grade students, and 26 nonresident students for grades 6-8 at Baker Middle School. Motion 14-015 approved Ms. Philippart's attendance at the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 2-4, 2014, and a further motion approved a Michigan Association of School Boards contract for the superintendent search following Dr. Fowler's announced June retirement. Mr. Schmidt referenced the $470 cut in the 2010 budget that the state has not restored. Closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c), began at 9:00 p.m. and the meeting reconvened at 9:03 p.m. Also attached are minutes of the January 7, January 20 and January 21 workshops, the last covering bond schematic design with TMP Architects, the Baker Middle School schedule and the bus purchase.

**Personnel.** A probationary contract for the remainder of the 2013-2014 school year for Danielle Andresen, .5 FTE ESL Teacher at Hamilton and Costello Elementary Schools: B.S., Wayne State University, Detroit, December 2005, elementary education major and social studies minor, Michigan Professional Certificate June 2011; ESL Teacher at National Heritage Academies, Pontiac, MI, August 2010 to February 2014; 3rd Grade Teacher at Academy of Oak Park-Marlow, August 2008 to June 2010; residing in Rochester Hills. Item 6.B is a negotiations update by Mr. Jasen Witt, Assistant Superintendent of Human Resources.

**Enrollment projections.** Dr. Fowler presents analysis by Dr. Frederick R. Ignatovich, Ph.D., of STANFRED Consultants, using birth data from the Michigan Department of Community Health and The National Center for Health Statistics. The birth-to-kindergarten ratio was 6.18 percent in 13-14, with 6.06 percent projected for 14-15. Schools of Choice students attending Troy grew from 287 in fall 2009/10 to 700 in 2012/13, while Troy residents attending other public districts numbered 242 in 2012/13; 2013/14 intake was 98 in kindergarten, 27 in first grade, 25 at Baker and 68 IAE freshmen. Projections exclude 224 students in ECP, SCSE and GROW programs and assume 50 Schools of Choice kindergarten and 30 first-grade students, in LOW, MOST LIKELY and HIGH sets. Projected total K-12 enrollment including SCSE, ECP and GROW is 12,653 for 2014/15, 12,665 for 2015/16, 12,699 for 2016/17, 12,746 for 2017/18 and 12,785 for 2018/19; a comparison slide shows projected 2013/14 enrollment of 12,444 against actual 12,573.

**Best Practices Incentive.** A resolution on the 2013-2014 Best Practices Incentive, Section 22f, with the Michigan Department of Education. Section 22f provides $52 per pupil one-time grants to districts satisfying at least 7 of 8 criteria not later than June 1, 2014 (MCL 388.1622f). Certified criteria: designated policy holder for medical benefit plans, 22f(1)(a); competitive bids on non-instructional services including custodial, transportation and food services, 22f(1)(b); nonresident applications under Section 105 or 105c (MCL 388.1705), 22f(1)(c); postsecondary credit opportunities, 22f(1)(e); online or blended learning with published course syllabi, 22f(1)(f); home-page link to the MiSchool Data Portal, 22f(1)(g); and health and physical education, 22f(1)(h). The secretary is directed to file the resolution with the State Aid and School Finance Office of the Michigan Department of Education; the roll call lists Schmidt, Underwood, Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Miletti and Philippart.

**Bus purchase.** Eighteen district school buses have reached end-of-life. MSBO Aggregate School Bus Purchasing Program pricing was extended by Thomas through February 15, 2014, and Mr. Dominick Asaro, Transportation Supervisor, compared Hoekstra (Thomas), Capital City (IC) and Holland (Bluebird). The resolution awards the bid to Hoekstra Transportation (Thomas) at $1,659,011.00 as an expenditure of the 2014 Capital Projects Fund; unit pricing is 2 conventional 36 passenger $170,802, 3 conventional 47 passenger $257,607, 3 conventional 47 passenger with lift $281,058, 6 conventional 77 passenger $503,424 and 4 transit 84 passenger $446,120. Competing totals were $1,659,658.00 from Capital City (IC), whose buses lack the Webasto TL17 engine pre-heater, and $1,699,087.00 from Holland (Bluebird). A February 4, 2014 memo from Mark S. Rajter to Dr. Barbara A. Fowler recommends replacing 18 units now, with one more later in the spring. The nine-year replacement forecast, base year 2013 plus 1.5 percent per year beyond 1/2014, shows Series 1 at 19 buses and $1,742,915, Series 2 at 25 buses and $2,311,759, Series 3 at 30 buses and $2,945,305, and 74 buses at $6,999,980 in total with estimated cost $5,257,065.

**Bond project timeline.** Dr. Fowler reviews Phase 1 of the 2013 Bond projects: secure entries at elementary and middle schools and IAE, a new collaboration center at Athens High School, a classroom addition and performing arts additions at Troy High School, vehicular site upgrades at 7 elementary schools, design sessions to develop schematic designs and cost estimates, and roofing at Larson Middle School and Hill Elementary.
